chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Isḥaq ibn Jarir from Abū Baṣīr said:

I heard Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) saying: 'The complete prayer (al-Imām) is performed in four places: in the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Ḥarām), the Mosque of the Messenger, the Mosque of Kūfah, and the Sanctuary of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him).'

And no one should say, on account of this report and the preceding report narrated by Ḥudhayfah ibn Manṣūr, that the complete prayer is restricted to the Sacred Mosque and the Mosque of Kūfah, so that when a person leaves them, there is no complete prayer, because it is not impossible that these two reports have been specific to the mention [of these two] for the sake of honoring them. Then, in other reports, phrases are mentioned in which these two mosques are included, even if the others are also included, and this is not improbable nor contradictory.

And we have previously presented from the reports that encompass the generality of places, among them these two mosques: The first report is from Ḥammād ibn 'Īsā from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) that he said: 'In the Sanctuary of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Sanctuary of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him).' And after it, the hadith of Ziyād al-Qandī that he said: 'Complete the prayer in the two Sanctuaries and in Kūfah,' and he did not say 'in the Mosque of Kūfah.'
As for what we presented from the reports regarding the inclusion of the mention of the two Sanctuaries in a general sense, they are more than can be counted.

And if it is established that the complete prayer in the Sanctuary of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is the preferred one rather than the mosque, based on specificity, and even if it was specific in these two reports, so too is it in the Mosque of Kūfah, because no one distinguished between the two places. And whoever is at 'Arafāt, it is not permissible for him to perform the complete prayer in any state, as narrated.

key_terms.الْإِتْمَام: Completing a short prayer (two rak'ahs) into a long prayer (four rak'ahs) while in a state of Ihram or other specific conditions.
key_terms.حَرَم: Sanctuary or sacred precinct, often referring to the broader sacred area surrounding a shrine or mosque.
key_terms.حَرَمُ الْحُسَيْنِ: The Sanctuary of Imām al--Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) in Karbala.
key_terms.عَرَفَات: The plain of 'Arafāt, a key site during Hajj.
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الرَّسُولِ: The Mosque of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in Medina.
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الْكُوفَةِ: The Mosque of Kūfah in Iraq.

ai.seo_question: What are the four places where the complete prayer (al-Imām) is performed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction between specific reports limiting 'al-Imām' to four locations and general reports by distinguishing between exclusive privilege and general permissibility, affirming the sanctity of Mecca, Medina, Kūfah, and Karbala. This scholarly synthesis underscores the Shia emphasis on the spiritual merit of the Ahl al-Bayt's shrines while maintaining that the ruling is not strictly confined to them. The exception of 'Arafāt highlights a unique jurisprudential nuance where the specific conditions for completing the prayer do not apply despite its status as a sacred site.
